expectations.text: Audience characterized at a useful specificity — narrow enough that some direction shapes are clearly right and some clearly wrong
expectations.evidence: Para 1: 'first-time manager 6–18 months into the role: recent enough that the work still feels unfamiliar, far enough in that the calendar is already structurally full of recurring 1:1s'; narrow enough to filter directions.

expectations.text: Current state of the landscape named — what tools or services the audience uses today, and the named ways those tools fail
expectations.evidence: Para 2 names three landscape categories with extensive product lists (Lighthouse, Lattice, 15Five, Culture Amp, Leapsome, Officevibe, Friday, Range, Soapbox/Hypercontext, Notion, etc.) and the specific failure mode of each category.

expectations.text: Real research signals only — aggregate signals, sourced findings, paraphrased user behavior; no fabricated quotes; no composite case studies with first-name attribution
expectations.evidence: Aggregate signals only; refers to 'practitioner-blog and Reddit r/managers patterns' as aggregate. No fabricated quotes or first-name composites.

expectations.text: Citations or (Inferred) markers on empirical claims — sources cited where claims are empirical; (Inferred) marks extensions
expectations.evidence: CCL, DDI, Gallup State of the American Workplace, HBR/Julia Rozovsky Project Aristotle, Marcus Buckingham/Manager Tools podcast cited; two (Inferred) markers explicitly flag extensions.

expectations.text: Source-quality hierarchy respected AND the highest-tier source available was reached for — primary government, peer-reviewed, or established non-profit sources used where they exist for this domain
expectations.evidence: Established research orgs (CCL, DDI, Gallup), HBR coverage of Project Aristotle and Buckingham; products only as landscape. No vendor blogs grounding foundational claims. Slightly weaker than with_skill (no Edmondson ASQ citation) but reaches highest tier reasonably available.

expectations.text: Strategic, not execution — every claim passes the operational test; no rendering-layer guidance appears
expectations.evidence: All claims affect direction choice (which moment to support, report-type variance, tooling-stack variance); no rendering or visual-design content.

expectations.text: No success criteria smuggled in — quantified targets and KPIs are absent
expectations.evidence: No quantified targets for the design appear. The Gallup framing is descriptive about the landscape.

expectations.text: No direction candidates smuggled in for the design — solution-shape proposals for the design are absent; landscape players (what the audience confronts today) is fine
expectations.evidence: Strategic-positioning paragraph names the gap (the 'before' moment, preparation vs capture) without proposing solution shapes. Landscape products are existing players the audience confronts.
